key_insight: CHORD introduces a universal generative pipeline that learns to choreograph 4D (3D + time) dynamics — modeling deformation, motion, and inter-object interactions — enabling scalable synthesis of complex scene behaviors without hand-crafted, category-specific rules.
problem_solved: Replaces labor-intensive, rule-based graphics heuristics by providing a learned, generalizable way to synthesize diverse dynamic objects and their interactions across categories in 4D scenes.
method: Object-centric 4D representation: encode objects with spatial and temporal structure to capture shape, pose, and deformation over time.
Learned dynamics & interaction module: predict temporal evolution and inter-object effects (collisions, contacts, coupled deformations) rather than relying on handcrafted rules.
Generative synthesis pipeline: produce realistic 4D scene sequences (trajectories + appearance) suitable for rendering, simulation, or downstream training.
impact: Makes generation of realistic, diverse dynamic scenes scalable for dataset creation, simulation, animation, and robotics, reducing manual effort and improving downstream model robustness to complex real-world dynamics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input object representations → dynamics/interaction module → 4D scene generator (clear module labels).
4D timeline/grid: sequences showing object deformation and interaction across time steps (before/after comparisons).
Interaction graph overlay: objects as nodes with arrows/forces illustrating predicted pairwise effects (collisions, pushes).
Qualitative mosaic: side-by-side CHORD outputs versus rule-based baselines to highlight diversity and realism.
paper_title: Choreographing a World of Dynamic Objects
paper_authors: Yanzhe Lyu, Chen Geng, Karthik Dharmarajan, Yunzhi Zhang, Hadi Alzayer
